text:
A: Hello! Hi! Can you hear me?
B: Yeah. Alright.
A: I'm Marisol, I'm in Leyton, East London. And you?
B: Dean. Gillingham. Kent.
A: Ah, Kent, okay. Not so far. Did you do the puzzle? I think I did it completely wrong, I was laughing at myself.
B: Yeah, did it. Dunno if it was right. Bit pointless, weren't it.
A: Ha, maybe a bit! So what do you do, Dean?
B: Er, admin. Sales and accounts at a plumbing supplies place in Rainham. Chasing invoices, purchase orders, answering the phone when the counter's busy. That's it really.
A: Oh, okay, so you are on the phone with the plumbers all day?
B: Pretty much, yeah. That bit I don't mind. They're alright, the trade lot, you know where you are with 'em. It's the paperwork I'm, er, not great at.
A: Ay, the paperwork. I am the same. I manage a shop in Walthamstow, a convenience store, twenty-two staff. I love the people, the customers, but the reports from head office, bueno, I do them at the last minute always.
B: Ha. Yeah, my manager Karen has to nag me every month end.
A: Every month I am Karen and also I am you! I nag the staff and then head office nags me.
B: Fair enough. Twenty-two's a lot of people.
A: It's a lot. This morning a delivery lorry was blocking the loading bay again, the driver was having a coffee, and I'm outside going, sorry, sorry, can you move please. And the new lad, lovely boy, but always late. Always.
B: We got a lad like that. Our coffee machine's been broke three weeks and nobody's fixed it, that's my big drama.
A: Three weeks with no coffee? No, no, that is a disaster. I'm from Colombia, coffee is very serious for me.
B: Ha, yeah, I bet. It's only instant anyway. Bit rank.
A: I have a moka pot at home, you can see it there behind me. Most coffee shops in London, I'm sorry, it's just hot brown water.
B: I just want something hot at half eight, mate, I'm not fussy.
A: Okay, okay, that's fair. You was saying, do you like the job?
B: Honestly? Not really. It's alright. Pays the rent. I'm part-time, which suits me. I keep saying I'll do a sparky course or gas or something, but, er, you know.
A: You know how it is. One day.
B: Yeah, one day. That's it really.
A: And football? I saw the cat behind you, but no football shirt.
B: Ha. Gillingham, unfortunately. Lost again Saturday. I go with my brother and moan the whole way home. Chelsea on telly 'cause of my dad.
A: Me, only Colombia. When there's a tournament I go to a Latin bar in Elephant and Castle with my friends and we scream at the TV. My husband is Portuguese, so when Colombia and Portugal play, it's very tense in my house.
B: Ha, I bet. Who wins?
A: In the house? Me, always. On the pitch, we don't talk about it.
B: Sounds like me and Gillingham, to be fair.
